questions.q: What exactly was the "ultraviolet catastrophe," and how did Planck's quantization fix it?
options: Classical physics predicted hot objects emit no light at all; Planck fixed it by adding electron orbits

Classical physics predicted hot objects should radiate infinite energy at high frequencies because every vibration mode gets equal thermal energy; Planck fixed it by requiring energy exchange in discrete chunks, which effectively shuts off the high-frequency modes
Classical physics predicted atoms would spiral into their nuclei instantly; Planck fixed it with discrete spectral lines
Classical physics predicted light travels slower than observed; Planck fixed it by quantizing speed
questions.explain: Equal energy sharing across the enormous number of high-frequency modes predicts (wrongly) infinite radiated energy at high frequencies. Planck's fix — energy exchanged only in discrete chunks sized to frequency — means high-frequency modes need a chunk too large for ordinary thermal energy to supply, so they stay unexcited and the catastrophe disappears.

questions.q: In the photoelectric effect, why does increasing the intensity of light below the threshold frequency never produce any photoelectrons, no matter how bright the light gets?
options: Because each photon's energy depends only on its frequency, not its intensity, so more too-weak photons arriving together still can't combine their energy on a single electron
Because bright light overheats the metal and destroys the electrons before they can escape
Because intensity and frequency are the same physical quantity in classical physics
Because photoelectrons only escape at night
questions.explain: Each photon delivers a fixed energy set by frequency alone. Below threshold, every individual photon is too weak to free an electron, and photons don't pool their energy onto one electron — so no amount of intensity (more too-weak photons) ever triggers emission. This is the opposite of what a continuous-wave theory of light predicts.

questions.q: Why do classical wave predictions for light fail to explain the sharp threshold-frequency behavior of the photoelectric effect?
options: Classical wave theory ties light's energy to intensity, not frequency, so it predicts brighter light should eventually eject electrons at any frequency — which contradicts the observed hard frequency cutoff
Classical wave theory has no concept of frequency at all
Classical wave theory predicts electrons are ejected only in darkness
Classical wave theory and Einstein's photon theory make identical predictions for this experiment
questions.explain: Classical electromagnetism says a wave's energy scales with intensity (amplitude squared), so turning up brightness should eventually supply enough energy regardless of color. Experiment shows a hard frequency cutoff instead, which only Einstein's per-photon quantized-energy picture explains.

questions.q: Why can't a classical model of an orbiting electron explain the sharp, discrete spectral lines emitted by a heated gas of a single element?
options: Classical mechanics predicts the electron should continuously radiate energy and spiral inward at a smoothly varying rate, giving a continuous smear of emitted frequencies, not a few sharp discrete lines
Classical mechanics predicts atoms cannot emit light under any circumstances
Classical mechanics predicts every element should produce an identical spectrum
Classical mechanics predicts spectral lines but gets their exact wavelengths right
questions.explain: An accelerating classical charge radiates continuously and should smoothly spiral into the nucleus, emitting a continuous range of frequencies along the way — not a handful of sharp, reproducible lines with dark gaps between them. Only restricting the electron to specific discrete energy levels, with photons emitted exactly at the energy gap between two levels, explains the observed discreteness.

questions.q: What single underlying assumption of classical physics do the ultraviolet catastrophe, the photoelectric effect, and atomic spectral lines all expose as wrong?
options: That light can travel through a vacuum
That energy and other physical quantities can take on any continuous value and evolve smoothly, rather than being restricted to discrete allowed values
That electrons have negative charge
That heat flows from hot objects to cold objects
questions.explain: All three phenomena only make sense once you drop the classical assumption of continuous, arbitrarily divisible energy: vibrational energy exchange, light energy per photon, and atomic energy levels all turn out to be quantized into discrete allowed values rather than continuous.
